instruction.text: Match the sounds and pictures to the correct punctuation marks.

atoms.sound: This punctuation mark connects two main clauses which are closely related.
This punctuation mark is used between two main clauses when the second clause expands on the information in the first.
This punctuation mark is used for a pause or break in the middle of a sentence.

instruction.text: Select the main clause that comes after the dash.

atoms.a: I need to hurry up – ((I don’t want to miss the bus.))
atoms.b: I need to hurry up – ((I don’t want to miss the bus.))

feedback.end: Dashes are used to separate two clauses. A dash adds a pause in the middle of the sentence.

hint.text: Dashes are used to separate two clauses. A dash adds a pause in the middle of the sentence.

instruction.text: Select the main clause that comes before the dash.

atoms.a: ((We just left to the cinema)) – I’ll see you soon.
atoms.b: ((We just left to the cinema)) – I’ll see you soon.

instruction.text: Select the main clause that comes after the colon

atoms.a: This house is so old: ((there’s so much history in the walls.))
atoms.b: This house is so old: ((there’s so much history in the walls.))

feedback.end: Colons can either introduce a list or expand on information in the clause before it. The first clause must be a main clause.

hint.text: Colons can either introduce a list or expand on information in the clause before it. The first clause must be a main clause.

instruction.text: Select the main clause that comes before the colon

atoms.a: ((We only have one chance to get the shot)): let’s make sure we’re ready to roll.
atoms.b: ((We only have one chance to get the shot)): let’s make sure we’re ready to roll.

instruction.text: Select the main clause that comes before the semi-colon.

atoms.a: ((My favourite subject is English)); my least favourite subject is Maths.
atoms.b: ((My favourite subject is English)); my least favourite subject is Maths.

feedback.end: Semi-colons can be used to join two independent clauses, without having to use a conjunction. They are like commas, but commas cannot be used between two main clauses.

hint.text: Semi-colons can be used to join two independent clauses, without having to use a conjunction. They are like commas, but commas cannot be used between two main clauses.

instruction.text: Select the main clause that comes after the semi-colon.

atoms.a: There’s traffic on the motorway; ((we should take a different route.))
atoms.b: There’s traffic on the motorway; ((we should take a different route.))
